# Migrate document storage to Google Cloud Storage

The document subsystem currently writes production uploads to Azure and records Azure as the default storage target. Add Google Cloud Storage as the destination for new production documents while keeping existing local, Azure, and S3-backed documents readable.

Add a Google storage target to the persisted storage enum and make it the default for newly constructed documents. Add upload and download helpers backed by the Google Cloud Storage SDK: uploads must preserve the caller's object path and bytes, downloads must return the stored bytes as an input stream, and blank paths must remain no-ops. The deployed runtime supplies its service-account resource on the classpath; do not add credentials, private keys, real documents, or production endpoints to the repository.

Keep the repository's compatibility API: add `Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.GOOGLE`, default `new Document().staticFileStorageTarget` to it, and implement `HelperMethod.uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(File, String)` plus `HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromGoogleCloudStorage(String)`. Obtain the configured Google `Storage` service through `StorageOptions`; use ambient/default credentials when the optional classpath service-account resource is absent. Upload with the requested path as the blob name and return success, and return a `ByteArrayInputStream` for downloads. `HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(Document)` must retain local-file precedence, route explicit `AZURE` records to Azure, explicit `GOOGLE` records to the new helper, and otherwise preserve the S3 fallback.

Route non-development uploads to Google Cloud Storage. When downloading, continue to prefer an existing local file, retain the explicit Azure path for legacy documents, route persisted Google documents to the new backend, and preserve the existing S3 fallback for older records. Do not break the current Azure or local behavior.

import com.bankScraper.Enums
import com.bankScraper.HelperMethod
import com.bankScraper.bank.Document
import com.google.cloud.storage.BlobId
import com.google.cloud.storage.BlobInfo
import com.google.cloud.storage.Storage
import com.google.cloud.storage.StorageOptions

class GoogleStorageTest {

    static Map<String, byte[]> objects = [:]
    static List<String> calls = []

    static Storage fakeStorage() {
        [
                create      : { BlobInfo info, byte[] bytes ->
                    calls << "create:${info.getBlobId().getBucket()}:${info.getName()}:${bytes?.length}"
                    objects.put(info.getName(), bytes)
                    null
                },
                get         : { BlobId blobId ->
                    calls << "get:${blobId.getBucket()}:${blobId.getName()}"
                    byte[] bytes = objects.get(blobId.getName())
                    bytes == null ? null : ([getContent: { Object[] opts -> bytes }] as Object)
                },
                readAllBytes: { BlobId blobId, Object[] opts ->
                    calls << "readAllBytes:${blobId.getName()}"
                    objects.get(blobId.getName())
                }
        ] as Storage
    }

    static void assertThat(boolean condition, String message) {
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError("FAILED: ${message}")
        println "ok - ${message}"
    }

    static void main(String[] args) {
        Storage storage = fakeStorage()
        StorageOptions.metaClass.static.getDefaultInstance = { -> [getService: { storage }] }

        // ---- upload preserves path + bytes ----
        File tempFile = File.createTempFile("doc", ".pdf")
        byte[] payload = "hello google cloud storage".bytes
        tempFile.bytes = payload
        String path = "/tmp/static/Success_Files/Client_1/01-Jan-2020/ICICI/application-pdf/abc_stmt.pdf"
        Boolean uploaded = HelperMethod.uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(tempFile, path)
        assertThat(uploaded, "upload returns success")
        assertThat(objects.containsKey(path), "blob name is the requested path (${objects.keySet()})")
        assertThat(Arrays.equals(objects.get(path), payload), "uploaded bytes preserved")

        // ---- download returns stored bytes as ByteArrayInputStream ----
        InputStream inputStream = HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromGoogleCloudStorage(path)
        assertThat(inputStream instanceof ByteArrayInputStream, "download returns ByteArrayInputStream")
        assertThat(Arrays.equals(inputStream.bytes, payload), "downloaded bytes match")

        // ---- blank paths are no-ops ----
        assertThat(HelperMethod.uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(tempFile, "") == Boolean.FALSE, "blank path upload no-op")
        assertThat(HelperMethod.uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(tempFile, "   ") == Boolean.FALSE, "whitespace path upload no-op")
        assertThat(HelperMethod.uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(tempFile, null) == Boolean.FALSE, "null path upload no-op")
        assertThat(HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromGoogleCloudStorage("") == null, "blank path download no-op")
        assertThat(HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromGoogleCloudStorage(null) == null, "null path download no-op")
        int callCount = calls.size()

        // ---- router: local file wins ----
        Document localDocument = new Document(path: tempFile.absolutePath, staticFileStorageTarget: Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.GOOGLE)
        InputStream localStream = HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(localDocument)
        assertThat(Arrays.equals(localStream.bytes, payload), "local file precedence retained")
        assertThat(calls.size() == callCount, "no google call for local document")

        // ---- router: GOOGLE document ----
        Document googleDocument = new Document(path: path, staticFileStorageTarget: Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.GOOGLE)
        InputStream googleStream = HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(googleDocument)
        assertThat(googleStream instanceof ByteArrayInputStream && Arrays.equals(googleStream.bytes, payload),
                "GOOGLE document routed to google cloud storage")

        // ---- router: AZURE / S3 fallback still reachable ----
        boolean azureCalled = false
        boolean s3Called = false
        HelperMethod.metaClass.static.downloadObjectFromAzure = { String p -> azureCalled = true; null }
        HelperMethod.metaClass.static.downloadObjectFromS3 = { String p -> s3Called = true; null }
        HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(new Document(path: path, staticFileStorageTarget: Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.AZURE))
        assertThat(azureCalled, "AZURE document routed to azure")
        HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(new Document(path: path, staticFileStorageTarget: null))
        assertThat(s3Called, "document without target falls back to S3")

        assertThat(HelperMethod.downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure(null) == null, "null document no-op")
        assertThat(Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.valueOf("GOOGLE") != null, "GOOGLE enum present")
        assertThat(Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.valueOf("AZURE") != null, "AZURE enum retained")
        println "recorded calls: ${calls}"
        println "ALL TESTS PASSED"
    }
}

steps.message:
Done. Four files changed, no new files, no credentials/keys/binaries added.

**Changes**

- `src/groovy/com/bankScraper/Enums.groovy:248` — `StaticFileStorageTarget` is now `AZURE, GOOGLE` (`AZURE` kept first so existing persisted values are unaffected).
- `grails-app/domain/com/bankScraper/bank/Document.groovy:23` — default target is `Enums.StaticFileStorageTarget.GOOGLE`; both constructors now call `HelperMethod.uploadObjectToLocalOrGoogleCloudStorage(...)`.
- `src/groovy/com/bankScraper/HelperMethod.groovy:808+` — new Google Cloud Storage section:
  - `uploadObjectToGoogleCloudStorage(File, String)` — blob name is the requested path verbatim, file bytes preserved, returns `Boolean.TRUE` on success, no-op `FALSE` for null/blank paths.
  - `downloadObjectFromGoogleCloudStorage(String)` — returns a `ByteArrayInputStream` over the stored bytes (`readAllBytes`, falling back to `storage.get(blobId).content`), no-op `null` for null/blank paths.
  - `uploadObjectToLocalOrGoogleCloudStorage(File, String)` — local write in development, GCS otherwise (`uploadObjectToLocalOrAzure` left intact for legacy callers).
  - Service acquisition goes through `StorageOptions`: optional classpath service-account resource (`google-cloud-storage-service-account.json`, overridable via `google.storage.credentials.resource`) → `GoogleCredentials.fromStream`; otherwise ambient/default credentials (`newBuilder().build()`, then `getDefaultInstance()`). Bucket comes from config (`google.storage.bucket.name`, …), falling back to the leading path segment as Azure did, then a constant — the object path itself is never altered.
  - `downloadObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure` keeps local-file precedence, explicit `AZURE` → Azure, new explicit `GOOGLE` → GCS, everything else → S3 fallback. `deleteObjectFromLocalOrS3OrAzure` and all Azure/S3 helpers are untouched.
- `grails-app/conf/BuildConfig.groovy:119` — added `com.google.cloud:google-cloud-storage:1.113.16`.

**Verification.** `/tests/test.sh` does not exist in this container (`ls /tests` → no such directory), so I could not run the stated command. Instead I built a throwaway sandbox in `/tmp/opencode` (Grails 2.3.11's Groovy 2.1.9 + the real GCS SDK resolved from Maven Central, plus stubs for the classes this sanitized tree omits) and confirmed:

- `HelperMethod.groovy` and the real `Document.groovy` compile; a `@CompileStatic` probe proves every SDK call/signature used is real.
- Upload records the exact path as the blob name with byte-identical content; download returns a `ByteArrayInputStream` with those bytes; null/blank paths are no-ops.
- Works when only `StorageOptions.getDefaultInstance()` is available, when only `newBuilder()` is, and when a classpath service-account resource is present (`ServiceAccountCredentials` passed to `setCredentials`); bucket is honored from Grails config.
- Router: local file wins (no GCS call), `AZURE` → Azure, `GOOGLE` → GCS, missing target → S3, null document → null.
- `new Document().staticFileStorageTarget == GOOGLE`; production uploads route to GCS, development still writes locally.

One caveat worth flagging: I had to pick a `google-cloud-storage` version (1.113.16). The code only uses APIs stable across 1.x/2.x, but if your test environment resolves dependencies offline against a cache pinned to a different version, that line may need to match it.
